events.text: At {wd_inn} three toughs from the river docks have the innkeeper by the collar over a bill they do not mean to pay. The other guests study their bowls. The innkeeper, an old woman with flour to the elbows, looks straight at you, the only stranger in the room.

effects.log: You stand. The toughs count your hands and your eyes and decide the bill can be paid after all. The innkeeper serves you the best bowl in the house.
You do not ask them to stop. The inn needs a new table, and the docks have three fewer teeth, and everyone on the road will hear of it.

choices.text: Keep your eyes on your bowl

effects.log: It is not your inn and not your fight. The toughs leave unpaid, and the innkeeper does not look at you again.

events.text: A cart has gone over in the yard of {wd_inn}, a mule screaming in the traces, a sack of rice burst open in the mud and a farmer's child pinned by the wheel. The yard is full of travellers. None of them moves.

effects.log: You set your shoulder to it and heave. The child crawls free. The farmer will not stop thanking you, and the whole inn buys you supper.
You make six travellers lift together. It works. They are all a little proud of themselves afterwards, and so are you.
Someone else lifts it eventually. You are already on the road.

events.text: The toughs troubling the innkeeper at {wd_inn} take one look at you and go very quiet. Your realm sits on you like a weight in the air, and even dock rats can feel it. The leader puts the money on the counter with both hands.

choices.text: Let them go with a warning

effects.log: They go, bowing. The innkeeper pours you tea with shaking hands and refuses your silver.
You make an example. The road will talk about it for a month, and so will the docks.

events.text: At {wd_inn} a merchant in silk is beating a serving boy for spilled tea. The room has gone quiet. The merchant notices your look, and laughs, and says something about knowing one's place.

effects.log: The merchant ends up in the horse trough. The serving boy brings you tea for the rest of the night and will not let you pay.

choices.text: Pay for the tea and say nothing

effects.log: You put a coin on the table for the spilled tea. The beating stops, if only because the merchant is confused.
The merchant buys you a cup. It tastes of nothing.

events.text: {npc} sits down across from you at {wd_inn} without asking, because every other table is full, and orders two bowls of noodles instead of one. "You look like someone with a long road behind you," {he} says. "So do I. Eat."

mem.note: shared a table and a long night of stories

effects.log: By the second pot of tea you have each told the other things you have told nobody. {npc} laughs like a door banging open.
{npc} does not mind. At dawn {he} pays for both bowls and is gone, leaving a note: "Same road, maybe."
{npc} shrugs and takes the noodles to the stairs.

events.text: At {wd_inn} the rain keeps everyone indoors for three days, and on the second day you and {npc}, a traveller with a battered sword case, start playing chess by the stove. By the third day the whole inn is watching, and neither of you has won a game.

effects.log: {npc} knows you let {him} win, and likes you better for it.

mem.note: lost a good game to you

effects.log: You win by a single stone. {npc} stares at the board, then laughs and demands another.

events.text: {npc} looks up when you come into {wd_inn}, and stares. "My grandmother told stories about {wd_past_title}," {he} says. "You walk the way the stories say. Forgive me. Sit, please, I am buying." Your soul hears that old name and turns over in its sleep.

effects.log: The stories are wrong in every detail and right in every way that matters. {npc} tells them with shining eyes.

choices.text: Say you have never heard the name

effects.log: {npc} looks disappointed, then sly. "Of course not," {he} says, and buys you a bowl anyway.

events.text: {npc}, a skinny young drifter with a stick for a sword, has been watching you eat at {wd_inn} for an hour. At last {he} comes over and kneels on the floorboards. "Teach me," {he} says. "Or let me carry your bags. I do not care which. I only want to go where you are going."

effects.log: You tell {npc} to get up off the floor. {He} follows you out into the morning, grinning.

mem.note: was given advice and a coin

effects.log: You tell {npc} where the honest schools are and give {him} silver for the road.
"Go home," you say. {npc} goes, slowly, looking back.

events.text: {npc} is sweeping the floor of {wd_inn} for a bowl of rice, and has been watching you since you came in. When you stand to go, {he} drops the broom. "I have heard of your sect," {he} says. "Everyone on this road has. Is it true you take anyone who will work?"

effects.log: You bring {npc} home. The gate guards look at the broom-callused hands and nod.

choices.text: Tell {him} the truth about the work

effects.log: You tell {npc} how hard it is. {He} listens to every word and is still there in the morning.

mem.note: was told there was no room

effects.log: {npc} picks the broom back up.

events.text: Two young drifters are fighting over the last bun at {wd_inn}, and the smaller one, {npc}, is winning, which is interesting. When it is over, {npc} gives the bun back to the bigger one. You watch {him} do it, and think of your own gate, and your own halls with room in them.

choices.text: Offer {npc} a place in your sect

mem.note: was offered a place in your sect

effects.log: {npc} stares, then bows so low {his} forehead hits the table. You have a new disciple, found on the road.
You buy a basket of buns. Both drifters remember you for years.

events.text: {npc} is singing in the corner of {wd_inn}, badly and happily, to a room that is pretending not to listen. When the song ends {he} catches you smiling, and comes over with {his} cup. "You laughed," {he} says. "At the song or at me?"

mem.note: talked until the lamps went out

effects.log: "Then you have no taste," {npc} says, sitting down, "and I like you anyway." You talk until the lamps go out.
{npc} looks at you a long moment, then laughs. "Good answer," {he} says.
{npc} shrugs, and starts another song.

events.text: The only seat left at {wd_inn} is beside {npc}, who has a map spread out over half the table and is arguing with it. "This road does not exist," {npc} says to you, as if you had been sitting there for hours. "I have walked it twice."

effects.log: You redraw the road together on the back of the menu. {npc} keeps the menu.
You trade roads until midnight. {npc} has walked farther than you, and listened better.

events.text: {npc} kicks your bench as {he} passes it at {wd_inn}, and does not apologise. "Nice sword," {he} says. "Shame about who is carrying it." The room goes quiet, waiting to see what kind of traveller you are.

effects.log: You laugh. It is the last thing {npc} expected, and {he} does not know what to do with it. {He} will remember that.

mem.note: was shamed in front of the inn

effects.log: The bench catches {npc} behind the knees. The room laughs. {npc} gets up red in the face and swears this is not over.

mem.note: gave you a name to remember

effects.log: "{npc}," {he} says. "Remember it." You will, as it turns out.

events.text: At {wd_inn} {npc} has beaten every guest at arm-wrestling and is looking for someone new. {His} eyes find you. {He} puts {his} elbow on your table and smiles with too many teeth.

effects.log: It goes on a long time. You win, barely, and {npc} looks at you as if you had stolen something.
{npc} tells the room you are afraid. Let {him}.

events.text: A blind storyteller at {wd_inn} tells of a swordswoman who walked from the western desert to the eastern sea without once sleeping under a roof. The guests argue over whether it is true. The storyteller only smiles and holds out a bowl.

choices.text: Put a coin in the bowl

effects.log: The storyteller tells you, privately, that the swordswoman slept in trees.

choices.text: Tell a tale of your own

effects.log: Your tale is shorter and duller, but the room is kind. The storyteller nods as if you had paid.

events.text: The innkeeper of {wd_inn} keeps a wall of names: every traveller who stayed a winter carved one into the beam above the stove. Some are so old that the wood has grown over them. The innkeeper hands you the knife.

effects.log: You carve it small, in a corner, between two names you do not know. It looks as if it has always been there.
You read them all. One of them makes you stop, for no reason you can name.

events.text: On the beam above the stove at {wd_inn}, among the names of old travellers, someone long ago carved "{wd_past_title}". The innkeeper notices you staring at it. "A legend of this road," the innkeeper says. "They say the one who carved it will come back someday and pay the bill."

effects.log: You pay a bill two lifetimes old. The innkeeper laughs, then stops laughing, and takes the money very carefully.

choices.text: Run your thumb over the name

effects.log: The cuts fit your hand. Something in you settles, like a traveller setting down a pack.

events.text: The champion of {wd_inn} is a vast cheerful ferryman who has never been beaten at the dumpling table, and by the twelfth bowl the whole inn is standing on the benches. By the twentieth the ferryman is asleep on the floor and you are still upright, more or less, and the room is chanting.

choices.text: Raise your teacup to the ferryman

effects.log: You toast the fallen champion. When the ferryman wakes, the first thing said is a laughing demand for a rematch next year.
You walk out in a perfect straight line, and then sit down very carefully in the yard where nobody can see, and loosen your belt.

events.text: You remember the fourteenth bowl. After the fifteenth you lie down, only for a moment. You wake in the stable of {wd_inn} with a mule looking at you and the inn's champion snoring in the next stall, and someone has drawn a moustache on your face in soot. You suspect the champion.

effects.log: The inn laughs with you, not at you, by the time you come back in. Mostly.
Fair is fair. The champion wakes, sees, and roars with laughter.

events.text: {npc} slams the bowl down across the table from you at {wd_inn}. "Again," {he} says, for the twentieth time. This time {his} chopsticks miss the dumpling. {npc} sits back, looks at the ceiling, and slides gently under the table, still glaring.

mem.note: was helped up from under the table

effects.log: {npc} lets you, and hates it, and does not hate you quite as much as before.
The inn steps over {npc} all evening. {He} will remember every step.

events.text: "Under the table," {npc} says, very pleased, "is where you belong." You would argue, but you are under the table, too full to move, and the floor of {wd_inn} is warm and very comfortable, and {npc} is eating one more dumpling just to show it can be done.

effects.log: "Next year," you say to the floor. {npc} laughs. It is almost friendly.
You swear it from the floor. {npc} eats to it.

events.text: The travelling musician at {wd_inn} plays first, a fast bright river tune, and the room claps. Then you play, something slow that you did not know you remembered. When you stop, nobody claps at all for a moment. Then the musician puts down the flute and bows to you.

effects.log: You bow to each other. The musician teaches you a new tune as payment for the old one.
The two of you play until dawn. The innkeeper gives you both free rooms.

events.text: The musician at {wd_inn} plays like water running downhill, and you play like someone carrying water uphill. The room is polite about it, which is worse. Afterwards the musician sits with you and shows you, kindly, where your fingers went wrong.

effects.log: You learn more in an hour of losing than in a year of practice.

choices.text: Ask for a rematch next year

effects.log: "Gladly," the musician says. "Practise the third bar."

events.text: {npc} plays first, fiercely and well, and stares at you the whole time. You answer with a tune that takes {his} melody and turns it gently inside out. By the end the room of {wd_inn} is humming your version, and {npc} is humming it too, furious.

effects.log: You play a duet. {npc} plays it beautifully, and pretends not to have enjoyed it.

mem.note: lost the duel before a crowd

effects.log: You take the applause. {npc} takes the door.

events.text: {npc} plays better, and both of you know it before the third bar. When the room of {wd_inn} applauds, {npc} leans over and says, quietly, "You were not bad. You were only second."

effects.log: {npc} looks startled, and then nods once.
You practise all night in the stable. {npc} hears it, and smiles in the dark.

events.text: You and {npc} buy a jar, three sticks of incense and a rooster's feather from a farm wife, and climb the hill behind the inn at sunset. Three bows to heaven, three to the earth. "Not born on the same day," {npc} says, "but on the same road." You say the rest of it together.

choices.text: Cut your palms and share the cup

mem.note: shared the cup of the oath

effects.log: A small cut, a shared cup. {npc} grins at you over the rim like someone who has finally come home.
"Whatever comes," you say. "Whatever comes," {npc} says back. It is enough.

events.text: {npc} kneels beside you on the hill and stops before the first bow. "They say you have done things," {he} says. "Hard things. I do not care. I am not swearing to the stories. I am swearing to you." Then {he} bows.

mem.note: swore to you, not the stories

effects.log: You bow together, three and three. Whatever you are, you are no longer alone on the road.

choices.text: Tell {npc} the worst of it first

mem.note: heard the worst of you and swore anyway

effects.log: You tell {npc} the worst. {He} listens, and bows anyway.

events.text: {npc}, your sworn sibling, rides into town with a cut over one eye and three bounty hunters a day behind. "I would not ask," {npc} says, "but you would never forgive me if I did not."

effects.log: You meet the bounty hunters in the road, together. They decide the bounty is not worth it.

choices.text: Hide {npc} and send the hunters astray

effects.log: You send the hunters three days the wrong way. {npc} sleeps in your loft and laughs about it for years.
You close the door. {npc} stands outside a long while before going. The road will hear of this.

events.text: A letter in {npc}'s untidy hand: "I am getting married at the new moon. You are the only family I have. If you are not there I will hold the wedding up until you come, and everyone will be very angry with you."

choices.text: Ride all night to get there

effects.log: You arrive at dawn, covered in dust. {npc} throws both arms around you in front of the whole wedding.

choices.text: Send a gift and your regrets

effects.log: The gift arrives. {npc} writes back a short, polite letter. It is the politeness that stings.

events.text: {npc}, your sworn sibling, finds you on the road with a jar of good wine and no reason at all. "The anniversary," {npc} says. "Of the hill. Or near enough. I lost count." You sit by the road until the stars come out, and talk about nothing and everything.

choices.text: Raise a cup to the oath

effects.log: You raise your cup to the hill, and to the road, and to whoever is still to come.
You hear everything, the good years and the bad. {npc} has been waiting to tell someone.

events.text: You bury {wd_sworn} on the hill behind an inn, because that is where the oath was sworn and where {wd_sworn} would have laughed to be buried. You pour out a cup for the earth and one for the sky. The road is very quiet.

choices.text: Carve the oath on the stone

effects.log: You carve the words you said together. Travellers stop to read them for years.
You walk on, because that is what the road is for. You leave the cup on the grave.

events.text: {npc} is waiting at the ford with {his} sword already drawn. "Every inn on this road tells your stories now," {he} says. "I am sick of them. Today the story ends."

ok.log: You beat {npc} in the shallows, and help {him} out of the water afterwards. {He} does not thank you.

fail.log: {npc} beats you in the shallows and walks away without a word, which is somehow worse.

effects.log: {npc} stares at you. Then, slowly, {he} sheathes the sword. "One meal," {he} says. It turns into a long night, and a friendship.

events.text: {npc} sends a letter instead of a challenge this time. "I am tired of hating you," it says. "It takes too much effort and the stories keep getting better for you. Meet me at the inn. I will pay."

effects.log: {npc} pays, as promised, and grumbles about it all night. By morning you are friends, more or less.

choices.text: Write back that you are busy

effects.log: {npc} reads the reply and tears it into very small pieces.

events.text: {npc}, whom you met at an inn and have not been able to stop thinking about, turns up at your door with two bowls of noodles and no excuse at all. "I was passing," {he} says. You live nowhere near anywhere.

effects.log: {npc} stays the season. By the end of it neither of you pretends it was a coincidence.
You eat together as friends. {npc} is a good friend. The look {he} gives you at the door says {he} hoped for more.

events.text: A letter comes from {npc}, whom you met on the road: three pages about rivers and inns and a dog {he} met, and at the very end, one line. "I keep wishing you were there to see it."

effects.log: You ride for a week. {npc} is standing at the river when you arrive, as if {he} knew.
You write back about your own rivers. The letters go on for years, warm and careful.

events.text: A storyteller at a crossroads inn is telling a story about {wd_title}, who drank a ferryman, a champion and a sworn enemy under the table in a single year and never once dropped a sword. You are sitting at the back. Nobody recognises you. The story is wildly wrong, and you are, apparently, a legend.

effects.log: It is not the name you were born with. It may be the one you are remembered by.
You laugh, and the road laughs with you, and the name follows you anyway.

events.text: You hear your own tune whistled by a farmer on a road you have never walked. The farmer learnt it from a pedlar, who heard it from {wd_title}, who, the pedlar swore, could make a stone weep with three notes.

effects.log: It is not the name you were born with. It may be the one you are remembered by.
You laugh, and the road laughs with you, and the name follows you anyway.

events.text: At an inn far from anywhere, a young traveller asks the innkeeper to point out {wd_title}. "The one whose sworn kin would cross a province for a letter," the young traveller says. The innkeeper points at you.

effects.log: It is not the name you were born with. It may be the one you are remembered by.
You laugh, and the road laughs with you, and the name follows you anyway.

events.text: The children of a roadside village have a game now: one plays the bully, one plays the innkeeper, and one, always the smallest, plays {wd_title}, who comes in out of the rain and makes it right.

effects.log: It is not the name you were born with. It may be the one you are remembered by.
You laugh, and the road laughs with you, and the name follows you anyway.

events.text: Innkeepers on three roads have started nailing their tables to the floor. Nobody says why. Everybody knows why. They are waiting for {wd_title}.

effects.log: It is not the name you were born with. It may be the one you are remembered by.
You laugh, and the road laughs with you, and the name follows you anyway.

events.text: A pedlar looks at your boots and your face and laughs. "I know you," the pedlar says. "Every inn from the desert to the sea knows you. {wd_title}, they call you. Is there a road you have not walked?"

effects.log: It is not the name you were born with. It may be the one you are remembered by.
You laugh, and the road laughs with you, and the name follows you anyway.
